verdicts.reason: The user at CLIENT01 starts the connection. rdp01.1sn0s.lab is labelled on the target. The caption matches the spec. The root vault seen in the background has no cables.
An amber pending pulse travels along the floor channel to the RDP server. Nothing is shown as trusted.
The pulse arrives at rdp01.1sn0s.lab and the listener lights. The server, not the client, is the owner.

The card is labelled 'Self-signed', not unsigned. The client tags it 'Unverified'. The channel stays amber and then dies out (strip frame 6 shows a grey channel), so the attempt ends. Minor: an amber square stays on the server front after the attempt has closed.
The RDPAuth badge drops from the direction of the AD node onto the server. The client channel is grey, so no connection is pending while the server enrolls.
Two keys form inside the server chassis: a padlock-headed private key and a ring-headed public key.
The padlock-headed private key drops into the safe-like key container (strip frame 2), and the lid closes and locks. The public key stays outside.
The ring public key enters the white capsule. The private key stays in its closed container. The caption matches the spec.
A light beam from the glowing container seals the capsule, leaving a band on it. No key-shaped object moves.

The capsule waits outside the server's outbound side, framed against the 1SN0S.LAB pillar. A small steel-blue query marker sits on AD (B-04.1_a). A cyan route lights toward Issuing CA 1 only. The capsule never enters AD.
The capsule travels along the lit cyan route into Issuing CA 1 only. It does not go near the root.

Only three of the four F-06 checks can be read. Check 1, 'Requester authenticated', is covered by the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label in every sampled frame, so the viewer never sees requester authentication. The capsule also sits over the 'Enroll permission' text.

The capsule is consumed before the press stamps, and it never reappears. CA 1's key module stays in place and drives the press. The card reads rdp01.1sn0s.lab / Remote Desktop Authentication, which is the correct EKU. The validity bar and the AIA/CDP ports cannot be made out at this tier (minor).
The card returns and docks beside the closed key container. The key does not move. CA 1's crown certificate stays in place. The separate translucent intermediate copy cannot be made out (minor).
The gold root vault sits on its own plinth with no cables. The self-seal ring is static, and the press and key module are dark.

The flashback is desaturated and labelled 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony', and the tag 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' is present. However, every flashback view of Issuing CA 1 still shows the present-day RDPAuth enrollment checks ('Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted', 'Request meets template policy'). That ties template-based end-entity enrollment to the setup ceremony. The cyan CA=true band on the CA request cannot be told apart in the desaturated grade.

The issuer link from Issuing CA 1's crown certificate to the root is drawn in bright neutral white, which is the request colour, not gold-to-cyan. In this colour language a white line ending at the root reads as something sent to the root. The root stays cable-free, and the caption is correct.

A new amber attempt starts. The server certificate and the CA 1 copy reach the client after the pulse arrives. No key-shaped object travels. The handshake-proof impression and the key pulse cannot be made out in any sampled frame (minor, verify).

The cards dock upward: server certificate, then CA 1, then the gold root in the cradle, with 'Installed earlier by policy'. Nothing travels from AD. Minor: the cradle reads dark grey until the shimmer.
The labels read 'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it' and 'Fetching never creates trust'. Nothing is fetched.
All six checks are listed: chain, signatures, validity, name rdp01.1sn0s.lab, EKU and revocation. Revocation shows as pending. Name match is a separate tick from chain building.
Two amber CRL fetches come from pki.1sn0s.lab and dock on the two non-root cards only, not the gold root. 'OCSP if deployed' sits on the client check list.
The channel turns green after all ticks pass. Minor: the caption fades in while the channel is still amber.
WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab is shown. The WebServer-TLS badge is largely hidden behind the WEB01 label (minor).
A local key pair forms. The private key is locked in its container, the public key goes into the capsule, and a beam seals the capsule.

A query marker goes to AD, and the capsule stays at WEB01. Issuing CA 1 is tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here'. Issuing CA 2 lights violet with the four eligibility tags. Minor: CA 1 still reads mostly cyan rather than muted grey.
The capsule travels along the violet route into Issuing CA 2 only.

Check 1, 'Requester authenticated', is again covered by the CA 2 label. The F-07 note 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is drawn on top of check 4 and neither can be read. That is the key compensating control for a subject-in-request template.

The capsule is consumed and the press stamps portal.1sn0s.lab / Server Authentication, which is the correct EKU. The card returns to WEB01 beside its container. The CA 2 intermediate copy cannot be made out (minor).
The CA 2 crown certificate already existed and the root stays dark, which is correct. But the link to the same root is drawn in request-white, not gold (the same defect as B-05.3).

An amber pulse goes to WEB01, the violet cards dock under the same gold root, the name/EKU/validity/revocation ticks resolve, and the channel turns green. The per-link CRL fetches and the proof impression cannot be made out in the sampled frames (minor).

The topology is right: root on top, two CAs, the servers under the CAs, and the root cable-free. But the paths converge at the root in white, the request colour, not gold. The user is not in the hero frame.
The title card matches the spec, followed by a clean fade to black.

findings.evidence: The '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' name plate sits directly over the first check row. Only fragments such as '...enticat' show, while 'Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted' and 'Request meets template policy' can be read. The white capsule also covers part of the 'Enroll permission' row.
findings.why: F-06 makes requester authentication the first of four distinct checks, and arriving at a CA is never sufficient. If check 1 cannot be read, the viewer sees a CA issuing without authenticating the requester.
findings.direction: Keep all four check rows clear of the CA name plate and the capsule for the whole hold, so each row is fully readable when its tick resolves.

findings.evidence: 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is drawn on the same line as 'Request meets template policy', and the two texts collide so neither can be read. Check 1 is again covered by the '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' plate.
findings.why: The restricted-Enroll note is the only on-screen statement of the F-07 control for a subject-in-request template. Without it, and without check 1, the beat suggests a CA issuing a requester-chosen name with no restriction or authentication.
findings.direction: Give the restriction note its own unobstructed position, separate from the four check rows, and keep the CA plate off check 1.

findings.evidence: Throughout the 'Earlier' flashback, Issuing CA 1's interior still shows the present-day RDPAuth check panel (template published, enroll permission, template policy). In the desaturated grade the CA request capsule shows no distinguishable CA=true band. Only the small text tag sets it apart (strip frame 2).
findings.why: These template checks belong to the later end-entity enrollment. Showing them during the setup ceremony mixes the RDP request's lifecycle into the root ceremony, which is the confusion PKI-S0R1-02 was meant to remove. AR-02 says the root never receives an end-entity request.
findings.direction: In the flashback, show Issuing CA 1 as it was at setup, without the RDPAuth check panel. Make the CA=true band readable within the desaturated grade, for example by luminance or shape, not hue alone.

findings.evidence: Every root-to-issuing-CA trust link (B-05.3, B-08.3, B-09.2, B-09.3) is drawn as a bright neutral white line. It is not gold-to-cyan, gold-to-violet or 'converging in gold'.
findings.why: White is the request colour. A white line ending at the root reads as something sent to the root, which runs against AR-02 (the root never receives an end-entity request) and undercuts the 'trust link, not a cable' meaning the spec requires.
findings.direction: Render the issuer links with the trust-link gradient the spec names: gold at the root, blending to cyan for CA 1 and violet for CA 2. Do not reuse request white.

findings.evidence: An amber pulse dot stays parked at the server end of channels that are already green (RDP after B-06.6, web after B-09.1). An amber square also stays on the RDP server front after the S2 attempt closes (strips/B-02.2_strip.png).
findings.why: Amber means pending. Leftover amber on validated or closed connections blurs the pending/validated distinction and the 'attempt ended' message.
findings.direction: Retire the pulse and listener amber when a connection closes or turns green.

findings.evidence: None of the sampled frames or strip frames shows the signature-impression handshake proof, the key pulse in the container, or the impression dissolving at the client. Only the two certificate cards are seen arriving.
findings.why: F-10 says a certificate alone proves nothing. If the proof of possession is too small or brief to see, the beat implies the cards alone authenticate the server.
findings.direction: Make the impression and its dissolve at the client readable at film scale, with the camera favouring it for a moment.

findings.evidence: The trust-store cradle reads as an empty dark-grey box while the chain docks. It turns gold only when 'Installed earlier by policy' appears.
findings.why: This can read as the root arriving or lighting up during chain building, rather than already being present (F-11).
findings.direction: Keep the gold root visibly in the cradle before docking begins. Let the shimmer be a highlight on a card that is already visible.

findings.evidence: After 'WebServer-TLS not published here', Issuing CA 1's vault still reads largely cyan rather than muted grey.
findings.why: Ineligibility is meant to be readable through colour as well as text.
findings.direction: Desaturate CA 1 fully to the ineligible grey token during the eligibility beat.

findings.evidence: The WebServer-TLS badge label is mostly hidden behind the WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab plates ('Web... LS').
findings.why: The template name is what drives CA eligibility in S7. If it cannot be read, F-14 is weaker.
findings.direction: Separate the template badge label from the host plates.

findings.evidence: Only one returning card can be made out. The translucent issuing-CA copy for the intermediate store is not distinguishable from it, for either server.
findings.why: The server's own intermediate copy explains what it presents in B-06.1 and B-09.1 (PKI-S0R2-01).
findings.direction: Make the translucent copy visibly separate as it settles into the intermediate store.
